text:
maya: Heads-up — Acme reported a weird SSE reconnect case where clients get duplicate partial outputs + sometimes a truncated final chunk. They say billing shows double tokens for the same user session :frowning_face:
acme_engineer: repro steps attached, happens reliably when their network blips for ~1-3s then reconnects. They use our resume-token flow and an idempotency header. Repro curl: 
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Idempotency-Key: 1234' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-x&resume_token=R-abc'
```
When they disconnect and reconnect with the resume_token, the client sometimes receives the last 2-3 tokens again, then a shortened tail. Billing shows the duplicate tokens charged.
maya: Thanks, can you paste the raw SSE stream fragments and the client logs?
acme_engineer: here, stripped: 
```
event: chunk
data: {"seq": 42, "text": "...your a"}

event: chunk
data: {"seq": 43, "text": "mazing respon"}

<disconnect>
(reconnect with resume_token R-abc)

event: chunk
data: {"seq": 42, "text": "...your a"}

event: chunk
data: {"seq": 43, "text": "mazing respon"}
event: chunk
data: {"seq": 44, "text": "se."}

<client shows final message as truncated: "...your amazing respon">
```
sam: interesting — seq numbers present but client still gets duplicates. are they using the official client or a custom SSE parser?
acme_engineer: custom. they do simple line-by-line parse, reassemble by seq but the seq resets in some reconnect cases? not sure.
eli: quick theory: server sends last N tokens on resume to guard against lost bytes; if client also replays buffered tokens or fails to persist last-ack, duplicates occur. two layers of replay => dup + sometimes truncated because the server's resume window overlaps an in-progress finalize step.
eli: need to know whether resume causes the server to send overlapping chunks or whether it starts from the exact next seq. can we get server logs for the session id?
maya: put this on eng-inbox. ops-bot: create incident.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-4121 (customer-stream-duplication). Assigned to eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:
julian: putting a small repro harness in /tmp. Node client snippet the customer used: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, {headers:{Authorization:`Bearer ${KEY}`, 'Idempotency-Key':'1234'}});
res.body.on('data', chunk => { /* naive append + split by "\n\n" */ });
```
julian: this naive split can lose partial lines and re-emit fragments on reconnect if not checkpointing last complete seq.
sam: ask runtime for: (1) server resume policy (how many tokens it rewinds), (2) whether resume emits identical seq IDs vs new ones, (3) whether we charge customers for retransmitted tokens on resume.
eli: quick look at runtime: resume currently rewinds by 1 token to ensure overlap for context continuity; seq IDs are stable per token but if model generation was mid-token when connection cut, the server may emit a partial final token. On resume we send the last stable token(s) again. That can look like dup if client already accepted them. Noted that billing currently counts emitted tokens per-client-connection, not deduped by resume.
ryan: billing note — duplicates currently bill. we need to decide if we credit or change counting semantics for resumed streams. will need finance signoff if we do retros.
maya: short-term: advise customer to checkpoint last confirmed seq client-side and on reconnect pass resume_token plus last_seq param. we can support `last_ack=43` to say "start after 43". Acme willing to patch client.
acme_engineer: can you confirm server will honor last_ack? we thought resume_token encapsulated that.
eli: server accepts optional `last_seen_seq` query param on resume; if present, we will avoid resending seq <= last_seen_seq. it's not in public docs, we'll add. internally flag to enable it for this customer now.
julian: also recommend client backoff/revive logic: wait for a single full blank-line separator before marking a chunk as "delivered" and persist last seq to disk ASAP.
maya: short-term plan: (1) enable last_seen_seq handling for Acme (2) patch docs and support article with Node/py examples (3) engineering: evaluate billing dedupe or retro credit for obvious duplicate-charge cases.
ryan: we can fast-track credits for affected customers — need list of request_ids + tokens charged. cc finance ops.
eli: long-term runtime change: switch to idempotent token accounting where each emitted chunk has a stable chunk-id which billing service dedupes. also extend resume to send explicit resume handshake with server-side ack of last_sent_seq to avoid ambiguity.
sam: assigning follow-ups: INC-4121 -> eng-runtime (eli), support article (julian), customer follow-up (maya), billing investigation (ryan).
maya: Acme wants a patch ETA. eli, how long to enable last_seen_seq and roll a patch to prod behind a feature flag?
eli: can do a guarded rollout in ~36-48h. will notify once enabled.
acme_engineer: amazing, thanks all. if you need more logs we can share full pcap of the reconnect window.
maya: grabbing pcap now and will upload to INC-4121. thanks everyone :pray:
